D5 — Which review mode should I run for the rest of this review?
Project/branch/task: plan-count fixture on `main`, PLAN.md "Add saved project views" under Approach B.
ELI10: The mode sets my posture for the 11 review sections. EXPANSION pushes scope up and recommends every extra enthusiastically. SELECTIVE EXPANSION holds the current scope as the baseline, reviews it rigorously, then shows you each extra (shared views, default view, keyboard shortcut, and so on) one at a time so you cherry-pick. HOLD SCOPE reviews only what's there and surfaces no extras. REDUCTION strips to the bare minimum. In every mode, every scope change is an individual opt-in; nothing is added or removed silently.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Too expansive and the pilot ships late with features nobody asked for; too narrow and obvious 30-minute wins (like shareable links) get missed.
Recommendation: SELECTIVE EXPANSION because this is a feature enhancement on an existing task list, and Approach B already produces a few cheap adjacent wins worth showing you individually.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Net: how much ambition I bring to the table versus how tightly I hold the plan as written. <gstack-qid:plan-ceo-review-mode>

options.label: SELECTIVE EXPANSION (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Full rigor on the accepted scope, plus each expansion candidate presented individually with neutral effort and risk. ✅ Rejected candidates land in NOT in scope, so nothing is lost or silently added. ❌ Adds several cherry-pick questions before the deep review starts.

options.label: SCOPE EXPANSION
options.description: ✅ Dreams big: 10x version, platonic ideal, and at least five delight items, each recommended enthusiastically. ✅ Best when you want this to become the flagship way people navigate tasks. ❌ Pushes toward shared views and a view platform the two-week pilot did not ask for.

options.label: HOLD SCOPE
options.description: ✅ Maximum rigor on Approach B exactly as approved; no expansion questions at all. ✅ Fastest path to a bulletproof, shippable plan. ❌ Cheap adjacent wins like shareable filter links never get surfaced for a decision.

options.label: SCOPE REDUCTION
options.description: ✅ Finds the absolute minimum that ships value, everything else deferred to follow-ups. ✅ Lowest pilot risk and smallest rollback surface. ❌ Likely cuts auto-restore or named views, undoing the reason Approach B was chosen.

projectedQuestions.question:
D7 — How should persisted filters remain readable?
Project: saved views, HOLD SCOPE.
Require a schema version and validation when a stored view is reopened.

D8 — What happens when a saved filter names a deleted label?
Project: saved views, HOLD SCOPE.
Show a clear warning for invalid clauses; never silently widen the result.

D9 — How should edits affect an applied saved view?
Project: saved views, HOLD SCOPE.
Require explicit Update or Save as new; silent overwrites destroy the saved definition.

D10 — How should an unauthorized saved view fail?
Project: saved views, HOLD SCOPE.
Return a visible error and preserve the current filters.
